From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-Interview: Senior Inference Engineer — scoring sync & late reviewers

Team — quick debrief on Alex Ng (onsite yesterday). I collected three full scorecards so far (technical, systems design, culture fit). Two people are late with numerical scores — Neha and Karthik, I see partial notes but no rubric numbers in the sheet.

High-level summary (from completed cards):
- Technical (coding + inference internals): median 6/10
- Systems design (distributed KV/cache, latency tradeoffs): median 7/10
- Culture / collaboration: median 8/10

Open items I want us to close before EOD:
1) Neha & Karthik: please enter your numeric scores in the shared scorecard (attached & sheet link below). We need final weighted average to decide on next step before Friday.
2) If scores remain split (variance > 1.5 pts across core areas) I propose a 30-minute tie-break sync today at 4pm PST to resolve.
3) Evidence to reference: resume-alex_ng.pdf, code-sample-output.txt, the small design diagram Alex sketched (attached in the scorecard file).

If you won't make the 4pm slot, flag here and add a quick 1-line justification in the rubric (confidence level + blocker). I can chair the tie-break if required.

Attachments: scorecard-alex_ng.xlsx, resume-alex_ng.pdf

Thanks —
Connor
Connor O'Brien
Hiring Manager, Inference Platform

My numbers (entered in the sheet and attached):
- Technical: 6.5/10 (struggled with micro-optimizations in the live problem, but had correct high-level approach)
- Systems design: 7.5/10 (solid tradeoff discussion, lacked depth on eviction/consistency under preemption)
- Culture: 8/10 (clear communicator, asked good clarifying Qs)

Notes / Tiebreak suggestion: If we end up close, prefer a short practical follow-up: 30-min home assignment (focused on a small cache-busting case) that we can grade pass/fail. It preserves momentum and gives objective signal.

I can make the 4pm slot. Uploaded scorecard-alex_ng.xlsx with my comments.

—Marissa

Subject: Re: Post-Interview: Senior Inference Engineer — scoring sync & late reviewers

Connor / team — my apologies for the delay, had back-to-back interviews this morning. I uploaded my numeric scores to the sheet at 4:40pm. Quick notes:

- My scores: Technical 7, Systems 7, Culture 7.5.
- Rationale: Alex showed practical experience with KV caching and cache-warm strategies we use; I think with a 2-week pairing we could close most of the perf gaps.

About normalization and decision: looking at submissions there is variance but not huge. If we apply Neha's recommended weight (45/35/20) the weighted average comes to ~6.6 — falls into "strong hire for IC3 with initial pairing" in our rubric.

Proposal: skip the home assignment and proceed with a short manager-level call to discuss ramp plan + compensation expectations if everyone agrees. If anyone still prefers the assignment, say so before 5:30pm and I'll defer to the group.

Link to final consolidated sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ZxY_example_sheet (I added a normalization tab).

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal SWE, Serving Runtime
